It has happened to them of the undesirable things. For Samaria has been destroyed, and the surrounding areas of the nations, Idumeans, Moabites, and those from Philistia, have trampled Judah. They have suffered many terrible things and have been tried by harsh days, both they and those. God will bring days that have not yet occurred, from the time when Ephraim separated from Judah. The king of the Assyrians, that is, Nebuchadnezzar, who destroyed Jerusalem and took all of Judah by force, burned the divine temple, and left nothing untouched, doing everything to the nation. And it will be on that day that the Lord will hiss to the flies, which rule over the part of the river of Egypt, and to the bee, which is in the land of the Assyrians. And all will come and rest in the clefts of the land, and in the holes of the rocks, and in the caves, and in every hollow tree.

Pharaoh Necho, king of Egypt, having left the one who was provoking, marched out with the entire army and was hastening against the land of the Assyrians. Josiah, being afraid that he might come against Judah, wanted to oppose him, although Pharaoh was dismissing the war against him. Rising up, he was killed in the war, and the Egyptian gained control of the land of the Judahites, and he came to such a degree of power that he even removed the reigning king, Joahaz, son of Josiah, and led him bound to his own land, and appointed Eliakim as king, and imposed taxes on the nation, and demanded a large collection of money. Then, Eliakim, having reigned over Judah for eleven full years, was succeeded by his son, Jehoiachin. After him, Zedekiah reigned, during whose reign Nebuchadnezzar campaigned against Judah, and having destroyed all, and added Jerusalem to the other cities, he took Israel captive, along with the vessels…

For Samaria has been destroyed, and the surrounding areas of the nations—Idumeans, Moabites, and those from Philistia—have trampled Judah. They have suffered many terrible things and have been tried by harsh days, both they and those. God will bring days that have not yet occurred, from the time when Ephraim separated from Judah (Hosea 8:9).

On that day, the Lord will hiss to the flies, which rule over the part of the river of Egypt, and to the bee, which is in the land of the Assyrians (Isaiah 7:18); and all will come and rest in the clefts of the land, and in the holes of the rocks, and in the caves, and in every hollow tree. The king of the Assyrians, that is, Nebuchadnezzar, who destroyed Jerusalem and took all of Judah by force, burned the divine temple, and left nothing untouched, doing everything to the nation. The narrative is being sharpened, and it penetrates thinly into the onset of the war, and that all their land, villages, and cities will be distributed among those who come against them at the designated times.
